subject: GreenCart — control plane needs for per-customer routing & quotas (discovery recap)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: GreenCart — control plane needs for per-customer routing & quotas (discovery recap)

Hi Emily — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have shared understanding and clear next steps.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Need deterministic per-customer QoS: customers in different tiers see different latency/throughput and higher-tier customers must be prioritized during contention.
- Hard and soft quota enforcement per account to prevent noisy neighbors and unexpected spend.
- Per-customer routing rules so we can route premium accounts to dedicated capacity or faster model variants.
- Auditability: token-level usage and per-request metadata available for monthly reconciliation and security reviews.

Current stack you mentioned:
- Ingest/gateway on AWS ALB -> internal routing -> ECS services calling an external model vendor today.
- Some in-house sharding by customer ID but no central policy engine for consistent rate/quota enforcement.

Success criteria you defined (you confirmed):
1) Ability to enforce tiered per-customer quotas with soft warnings + hard cutoff.
2) Route 99% of premium customer requests to dedicated/pinned capacity with fallback to shared capacity under pressure.
3) Audit logs + per-tenant usage export in CSV/BigQuery for billing.
4) Pilot within 3–4 weeks and production rollout within ~8–10 weeks once SLOs met.

Suggested next steps (please confirm or edit):
- I will share a proposed control matrix (attached) mapping GreenCart tiers -> routing policy, quotas, and fallbacks.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Rishi (our inference/ops lead) to validate cache isolation, rate limiter semantics, and KV cache behavior.
- Procurement touchpoint to discuss contract terms and pilot scope (CC’ing procurement if helpful).

Action items from us:
- Attach: greencart-control-matrix.xlsx (control plane mapping) and Redwood one-pager.
- Tech deep-dive: propose Wed 10/14 10:00–11:00 PT.
- High-level pilot proposal & SOW draft to be shared by 10/15.

Emily, anything I missed or that you’d re-prioritize? If the Wed slot works I’ll send a calendar invite and include Rishi & Laura.

Best,
Monica

Subject: Re: GreenCart — control plane needs for per-customer routing & quotas (discovery recap)

Thanks Monica — this is a clean summary and captures our concerns. A couple clarifying items from our side: 

- Quota enforcement model: we want both soft limits (alerts + admin override) and hard limits (reject) configurable per-tier. Can Redwood express both behaviors per policy?
- KV cache isolation: we can’t have cross-tenant leakage of cached prompts/keys. Is that isolation per customer or per-tenant group?
- SLA question: for premium tier routing you mentioned "route to dedicated capacity" — what happens if dedicated pool is saturated? We need deterministic fallback that keeps latency bounded.

Procurement: we’d like a rough cost estimate for a 2-week pilot (10k requests/day, mixed traffic) and an example SOW template if you have it.

If Wed 10/14 10:00 PT works, include Rishi — we can bring our infra lead (Samir) to the call for the cache isolation piece.

—Emily

Subject: Re: GreenCart — control plane needs for per-customer routing & quotas (discovery recap)

Emily — quick technical notes ahead of Wed’s deep-dive, to reassure on the items you called out.

- Soft vs hard limits: Redwood supports policy-level actions. Each quota policy can emit a configurable soft threshold (emit webhook / alert + add response header) and a hard threshold (HTTP 429 or reject). These are per-customer policies and evaluated in the control plane before dispatch to the runtime.

- KV cache isolation: we provide per-customer/tenant namespaces for KV caches and prefix-based keying. No shared in-memory caches across tenant namespaces; we also support optional encryption of cached values with customer-specific key IDs.

- Dedicated pool saturation/fallback: policy language allows specifying a fallback route chain. Typical pattern we recommend: 1) preferential routing to dedicated pool; 2) if latency or queue depth exceeds threshold, automatically route to a dedicated-but-smaller ultra-low-cost model variant in shared pool; 3) final fallback to a controlled rejection with a friendly user-facing message. All of this is observable in our console so you can tune thresholds.

- Auditability & billing: per-request token usage is emitted as events and aggregated per-customer. We can export CSV or push to your BigQuery project via a service account.

Rough pilot estimate (ballpark):
- 2-week pilot, reserve 2x baseline capacity for headroom: estimated cloud infra + Redwood managed controls = ~$6,500–9,000 (depends on exact qps pattern). I’ll convert this into a line-item pilot quote for procurement.

I attached the control matrix with technical mappings and a simple flow diagram. For Wed’s call, I’ll walk through the cache isolation and rate-limiter internals.

Cheers,
Rishi
